defects.title: Edge weights are shifted when a metabolite lies off the cycle
defects.trigger: 3 metabolites A,B,C with inclusion rates A 0.5, B 1, C 0.25 and an MTG where A is not on the path from C to B (see notes)
defects.observed: G.Edges = two edges (2,3) with mets C and B and Weight 0.25 and 0.5: B carries A's rate; line 66 filters inclusionOrder before line 67 builds the mask for A, so A keeps its first entries; both stay filtered for later starting nodes
defects.expected: B with its own inclusion rate 1 (inclusionOrder and A filtered with one mask from the unfiltered lists)

notes: Reproduction (MATLAB): model.mets = {'A';'B';'C'}; BG = graph([], [], [], 7); BG.Nodes.mets = {'A';'A';'B';'C';'C';'C';'C'}; arm.L = sparse([2 1 4]); arm.I2A = sparse(ones(1,7)); arm.ATG = graph([], [], [], 7); arm.ATG.Nodes.MoietyIndex = (1:7)'; MTG = graph([1 3], [2 2], [], 3); MTG.Nodes.IsomorphismClass = [1;1;1]; MTG.Nodes.mets = {'A';'B';'C'}; MTG.Nodes.MoietyIndex = [1;2;3]; arm.MTG = MTG; G = createMoietyGraph(model, BG, arm); G.Edges -> rows (2,3) C 0.25 and (2,3) B 0.5. With MTG = graph([1 1],[2 3],[],3) (all on the path) the weights match the rates. Callee getMetMoietySubgraphs is called once per class (line 36) with the same result; no defect there. Callers: only testConservedReactingMoieties (multi-function test) and a tutorial.
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproduction: a metabolite not on the cycle shifts edge weights to the wrong metabolites, lines 66-67)

defects.title: A model without any gene rule stops with an error
defects.trigger: readGeneRules(model) with every grRules entry empty
defects.observed: error "Unrecognized function or variable 'term2'." at line 115

notes: Reproduction (MATLAB, in a temporary folder because line 78 saves readGeneRules.mat into the current folder before its error): m.rxns = {'r1'}; m.genes = {'b3925';'b4232'}; m.grRules = {'(b3925 or b4232)'}; readGeneRules(m) -> error at line 83; readGeneRules(getDistributedModel('ecoli_core_model.mat')) -> same error (consistent with testGeneReactionMILP's header). Second defect: the 5-rule model of the trigger. Other observations: term.function is a 1x1 cell for and/or but char for 'equal'; 'g1 and g2 or g3' (mixed operators without parentheses) errors by design at line 79 ('Boolean functions are inappropriate.'). Callers reaching the error defect: gDel_minRN (line 114) and step2and3 (line 91) for any model with such a rule; reactionKO2term is returned by both callers' calls but not used further.
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproduction: any parenthesised rule stops at line 83, so ecoli_core_model fails; reactionKO2term points to the wrong terms)

defects.title: k.mat and nSets.mat are not written
defects.trigger: saveInputsOptForce(model, {'R2'}, {'R1'}, {'R2'}, [0;-5], [10;0], [1;-5], [10;-1], 3, 2, struct('rxnList', {{'R1'}}, 'values', 1), {}, {}, {}, folder) with the createModel model of the notes
defects.observed: folder holds 12 files (constrOpt, excludedK/L/URxns, maxFluxesM/W, minFluxesM/W, model, mustL, mustU, targetRxn .mat); exist(k.mat) = 0, exist(nSets.mat) = 0 (lines 136-147 never save k or nSets)
defects.expected: k.mat and nSets.mat written as the OUTPUTS section documents

notes: Reproduction (MATLAB): model = createModel({'R1'; 'R2'}, {'first'; 'second'}, {'a -> b'; 'b <=> '}, 'printLevel', 0); w = tempname; saveInputsOptForce(model, {'R2'}, {'R1'}, {'R2'}, [0;-5], [10;0], [1;-5], [10;-1], 3, 2, struct('rxnList', {{'R1'}}, 'values', 1), {}, {}, {}, w); exist(fullfile(w,'k.mat'),'file') -> 0. Severity is a judgement (documented output missing, by analogy with 'last sample not written' = wrong-result); if the lead rates it cosmetic (doc-only), the function is otherwise straightforward to test like the two Must-set savers. Caller reaching it: optForce with keepInputs = true (lines 385, 575).
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproduction: the documented outputs k.mat and nSets.mat are never written)
